summary: The Sea Crown: the northern maritime crown of the East, anchor of the Noris Treaty, watching a northern sea where lights have begun to appear.

lorvenas_court_spirit.name: Lorvena's Court
lorvenas_court_spirit.desc: The queen's court stands above the quays, and its windows face the northern sea. Captains are welcome at her table; courtiers who have never smelled tar are not.

northern_shore_crown.name: Crown of the Northern Shore
northern_shore_crown.desc: Lorvena wears a crown of grey pearl and dark silver, and the harbours of the north answer to her. A captain who sails under her flag has the best charts and the longest memory in the East.

northern_sea_masters.name: Masters of the Northern Sea
northern_sea_masters.desc: No ship sails the northern coast without being noted by a Gondolin watcher, and no storm surprises a Gondolin captain. The coasters call the queen's captains the sea's own.

watchers_of_gondolin.name: The Watchers of Gondolin
watchers_of_gondolin.desc: Lookouts on every headland keep a log of every sail and an eye on every shadow. A quiet sea is no reason to sleep.

stand_against_the_tide.name: Stand Against the Tide
stand_against_the_tide.desc: The northern shore has seen what comes out of the dark water, and Gondolin has chosen to meet it on the sand. Every fisher and farmer knows where to stand when the horn blows.

lights_beyond_the_islands.title: Lights Beyond the Islands
lights_beyond_the_islands.desc: Lookouts on the northern headland report lights where no harbour stands, small and pale and far from any known shore. The old fishers say they are lamps, and the young lookouts are not so sure.

royal_house_of_gondolin.title: The Royal House of Gondolin
royal_house_of_gondolin.desc: Queen Lorvena has no heir, and her council has begun to speak of a match. Furvior has sent letters, her captains have sent poems, and the old houses of the northern shore have sent their sons.

lights_on_far_shores.title: Lights Beyond the Islands
lights_on_far_shores.desc: The lights beyond the islands are no longer a story. Fishers tell of dead men on far shores, of black hulls under dark sails and of a cold that comes before them. The queen's council sits all night and speaks of nothing else.

focuses.name: The Sea Crown
focuses.desc: Gondolin's queens have ruled the northern coast from a hall above the salt quays. Lorvena is proud of the Treaty and prouder of her captains.

focuses.name: Lorvena's Court
focuses.desc: The queen's court is a sea-hall of dark timber and grey stone. Its walls are hung with charts, and its tables are set with maps instead of cloths.

focuses.name: The Northern Houses
focuses.desc: The houses of the northern shore sit on the queen's council, each with a harbour, a fleet of boats and a quarrel. Lorvena keeps the peace by remembering all of them.

focuses.name: The Royal House of Gondolin
focuses.desc: The question of the succession is raised in council and not answered. The queen's captains, the houses and the allies in Furvior each have a candidate.

focuses.name: The Queen's Council
focuses.desc: The queen sets up a council of captains and shipwrights, who meet monthly in the harbour hall. They advise her on tides, timber and the price of rope.

focuses.name: Crown of the Northern Shore
focuses.desc: Lorvena is crowned again at the midwinter fair, with pearls from the northern beds and silver from the Salt Road. Fishers and captains cheer from the quay.

focuses.name: Harbours of Gondolin
focuses.desc: Stone moles reach out from every cove, and a breakwater is begun at the largest. A shipyard rises beside the fish-market, and its hammers never stop.

focuses.name: The Salt Quays
focuses.desc: Noris's salt comes up the Salt Road in sacks and goes out by sea in barrels, and every barrel pays a coin at the quays. The harbour master keeps the books himself.

focuses.name: Galleys of Gondolin
focuses.desc: Long, narrow galleys are built for the northern coast, fast under oars and steady in a swell. The yard-masters carve the queen's sign on every prow.

focuses.name: The Fishing Fleets
focuses.desc: Fishing fleets sail with the dawn tide and return with the dusk, and the catch is salted on the quay. A good year feeds half the northern coast.

focuses.name: Sea Charts of the North
focuses.desc: Captains copy their logs into a single chart-book, kept at the harbour hall and updated each season. A ship without a chart is a lost ship, and Gondolin loses few.

focuses.name: Warships of the North
focuses.desc: Two-masted warships with iron rams and fighting-tops are laid down in the yards, built to hold the northern waves. Their keels are cut from the best timber of the coast.

focuses.name: Masters of the Northern Sea
focuses.desc: A war-fleet stands in the northern roads under the queen's banner, and the coasters call her captains the sea's own. Few vessels dare the channel without leave.

focuses.name: Watch on the Northern Sea
focuses.desc: Beacon towers rise on every headland, each with a keeper and a log. The queen asks that every light, every sail and every odd shadow be written down.

focuses.name: The Watchers of Gondolin
focuses.desc: The watchers are drawn from old fishing families, who know the sea by its sound. They are posted in pairs, and no pair is allowed to sleep at once.

focuses.name: Beacons of the Shore
focuses.desc: A chain of beacons is raised along the whole northern shore, each in sight of the next. A flame at one end of the coast is seen at the other within the hour.

focuses.name: Word to Furvior
focuses.desc: A rider is sent over the Salt Road with a sealed report for Noris's court. Lorvena asks her ally to read it with care and answer it without delay.

focuses.name: The Dead on the Shore
focuses.desc: The dead have come out of the northern sea, and the beacons burn from end to end of the coast. Gondolin's fishers and farmers take up their spears and stand on the sand.

focuses.name: Ships Against the Black Sails
focuses.desc: Every hull that can carry a ram is sent to the northern roads, and the captains are told to sink black sails and spare nothing else. The queen herself watches the first fleet leave.

focuses.name: Northern Anchor of the Treaty
focuses.desc: Gondolin has been Furvior's partner in the Noris Treaty for generations, and its quays carry the Treaty's salt. The queen takes the title of anchor with pride.

focuses.name: The Salt Road's End
focuses.desc: The Salt Road ends at the sea, and its last miles are paved and lit. Everything that comes down it is weighed, marked and shipped within a day.

focuses.name: Treaty Levies of Gondolin
focuses.desc: Spearmen of the northern shore are sent to Furvior to drill beside the Treaty's riders. They return seasick and wiser.

focuses.name: A Voice in the Treaty Council
focuses.desc: Gondolin asks for a seat at the Treaty's table and a vote on its roads. Noris's riders are not used to being asked, and listen.

focuses.name: Ask More of Furvior
focuses.desc: Gondolin asks for a larger share of the salt trade and a subsidy for its yards. Furvior's court sighs, haggles and pays a little.
